notes: §1985:X.1.3.8.1 SR1: the name of a non-common program 'directly contained within another program ... may be referenced only by statements included in that containing program'; any other program's CALL or CANCEL of that name names a different program (§1985:X.5.2.4 GR4 c) or none, so the rule is a run-time resolution, not a refusal. ProgramTable#ResolveVisible, which CALL and Cancel share, admits a contained program only as a child of the caller (rule 1), a COMMON sibling of an ancestor (rule 3) or the caller itself when RECURSIVE (unreachable at 85: RECURSIVE refused, COBOL0885), otherwise an outermost program; BinderDriver#MakeUnit registers each program's containment path. Probes at --std 85: a sibling's CALL of the non-common INNER reached the separately compiled INNER of the same name and its CANCEL left the nested INNER's count intact (3 on the next call from OUTER); OUTER's CALL of grandchild LEAF, by literal and by identifier, took ON EXCEPTION while MID reached it; a sibling's CALL of non-common MID took ON EXCEPTION. The witness shows a sibling's CALL of a non-common nested program failing.

next.reason: 1985: a non-common directly contained program-name 'may be referenced only by statements included in that containing program'. 2023 §2023:8.4.6.3 SR1 keeps that and adds 'or, if the program possesses the recursive attribute, in the program itself'; §2023:11.10.4 GR4: a recursive program 'may call itself'. Looser: a new permitted reference (RECURSIVE did not exist in 1985, so conforming 1985 programs are unaffected).
